subject: Praxis Financial — failover orchestration and RTO/RPO clarifications
messages:
From: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@praxisfinancial.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Cho <alan.cho@praxisfinancial.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@praxisfinancial.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP — DR orchestration questions (RTO/RPO, session continuity)

Hannah,

Thanks for the initial questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our resilience team so we can map Praxis' regulatory requirements to your offering:

1) For multi-region failover, what is the committed RTO and RPO for stateful inference workloads (i.e., sessions with KV cache per user)?
2) How do you handle in-flight requests during a regional outage — do you drain, retry, or redirect, and what guarantees exist for idempotency?
3) Do you provide a documented orchestration playbook we can test against (playback of failover rehearsals)? Any constraints for data retention during failover (temporary logs, egress)?
4) If we run Dedicated capacity in our VPC, how are key materials and logs handled during cross-region failover (KMS/HSM handoff)?

We need concrete sequence steps and any evidence artifacts (runbook excerpts, rehearsal witnesses) to include with our submission. Can you provide by next Wednesday?

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lopez
Director, Resilience & Ops — Praxis Financial

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@praxisfinancial.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — DR orchestration questions (RTO/RPO, session continuity)

Samantha —

Thanks, read through your four points and good questions. High level answers below; attaching a short orchestration whitepaper and a runbook excerpt. We'll follow up with a sequencing table and a reproducible rehearsal checklist.

1) Committed RTO/RPO (hosted + dedicated):
- RTO: Target 3 minutes for stateless requests under our Hosted SLA; 15 minutes for stateful sessions where customers run on Dedicated with cross-region replication turned on.
- RPO: Near-zero for cached KV if you opt into our automatic cross-region KV replication option; otherwise up to 30s for asynchronous replication mode.

2) In-flight request handling:
- Default: short draining window (30s) then redirect to secondary region with automatic request replay where safe.
- Idempotency: we recommend idempotency tokens for any client action; our runtime supports replay-safe endpoints for generation and a best-effort de-duplication layer.

3) Orchestration playbook and rehearsals:
- Attached: redwood_failover_orchestration.pdf (overview) and runbook_sequence_excerpt.md (playbook snippet).
- We run quarterly rehearsals for Dedicated customers; evidence includes rehearsal logs and a BIA matrix excerpt (attached).

4) Keys/logs handling for Dedicated in VPC:
- KMS/HSM: customer-controlled KMS is used; during regional failover we use per-region KMS endpoints with no plaintext key movement. HSM-backed keys remain in customer VPC/HSM.
- Logs: control-plane diagnostics are mirrored to a customer-controlled S3 bucket (configurable retention). During failover, we provide time-bounded snapshot exports.

I'll loop in Grace (Product) and Markus (Infra) for technical sequencing. If you can list the specific test cases you want exercised, we'll map them to our rehearsal checklist.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_failover_orchestration.pdf; runbook_sequence_excerpt.md; BIA_matrix_v2.xlsx; SOC2-type2-cert.pdf

From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@praxisfinancial.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@praxisfinancial.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — follow-up on session continuity behavior

Hannah/Grace,

Thanks for the doc. A narrow clarification: our use case has long-lived interactive sessions (~20–30 minutes) with per-session KV (partial chat history + user profile). If the primary region fails and we redirect to secondary, will the session resume seamlessly from the latest persisted KV, or is there a window where we can expect duplication/loss? We need to quantify expected user-visible anomalies per rehearsal.

Also, can you confirm the retention policy for temporary request logs during failover? (Praxis cannot accept more than 90 days retention for ephemeral logs.)

Alan
Sr. Manager, Resilience Engineering — Praxis Financial

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@praxisfinancial.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — follow-up on session continuity behavior

Alan —

Short answer: with cross-region KV replication enabled and the Dedicated replay pipeline configured, sessions resume with session continuity in >99% of rehearsals. A few implementation details to set expectations: 

- Replication model: we offer synchronous replication for KV namespaces where customers require sub-second RPO. Synchronous mode requires a small latency tradeoff; typical added tail latency is ~8–12ms.
- Asynchronous fallback: if synchronous replication isn't enabled, the system will roll-forward and reconcile; expected user-visible duplication is minimal but can occur for the last 1–3 requests in a failover window in our tests.
- Rehearsal metrics: our quarterly DR rehearsals track continuity_rate (successful seamless resumes), duplication_events_per_1000, and mean_catchup_seconds. Example excerpt (from attached BIA_matrix_v2.xlsx): continuity_rate 99.4%, duplication_events 0.7/1000, mean_catchup 4.1s.

Temporary logs retention: we can cap ephemeral diagnostic logs to <= 90 days. Control-plane audit logs follow customer policy; we provide secure exports and redaction tooling.

I've pasted a short runbook sequence below for clarity:

--- runbook excerpt (abridged) ---
1) Detect region health anomaly via multi-channel probes (SLA monitor + infra alarms).
2) Trigger controlled drain on primary serving cluster (30s drain window).
3) Snapshot KV namespaces to replicated store and confirm last-consistent sequence id.
4) Promote secondary cluster; apply last-consistent sequence id and reconcile pending writes.
5) Route client traffic to secondary; enable replay pipeline for idempotent endpoints.
6) Post-failover validation (consistency checks + smoke tests); publish rehearsal artifacts to shared drive.
--- end excerpt ---

If Praxis wants, we can run a dedicated rehearsal with you and provide a signed witness statement from our ops team.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Product Manager, Resilience — Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@praxisfinancial.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — technical sequencing and evidence artifacts

Alan —

Couple of technical notes and reproducible test items we recommend for your RFP evidence pack: 

- Test case A (Synchronous KV): run a failover while measuring sequence id handoff — expected RTO ~7–12m for stateful switchover in a controlled drill, measured under our Dedicated hardware profile.
- Test case B (Async KV with replay): measure duplication and catch-up; we provide scripts that generate session load and a post-run reconciliation report.
- Evidence artifacts we will supply: rehearsal logs (timestamped events), reconciliation reports (per-namespace), runbook signed by on-call witnesses, and a short video screen capture of control-plane promotion steps.

Also: when using customer-managed KMS, there is no key export during failover; each region references the customer KMS endpoint — we will provide a written attestation for your procurement file.

I'll drop the recommended test scripts to the shared drive link and coordinate dates once Praxis confirms the rehearsal window.

-Markus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Team —

Action items we have recorded:
- Redwood to deliver rehearsal checklist + test scripts (shared drive link) by 2026-08-25.
- Redwood to provide KMS attestation doc and signed runbook excerpt by 2026-09-01.
- Praxis to confirm rehearsal window and provide contact for on-site witness.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Samantha
